vopros: My site blocks AI crawlers. Who can check it and open it up so AI assistants can see my business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
You’re looking for a **technical SEO or AI-search (AEO/GEO) specialist**—ideally someone who can audit and change the site, not just provide a visibility report. Ask them to check:

- `robots.txt` rules for relevant crawlers, such as **OAI-SearchBot / GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, and Google-Extended**
- Blocking by your hosting provider, CDN, firewall, or bot-protection settings
- Whether important pages render readable content without relying on JavaScript
- Sitemaps, page indexing settings, and structured data

A crawler-access checker can give you a quick initial read of the public `robots.txt` rules; the search results included options such as Apify’s **AI Crawler Access Checker**. But a checker usually can’t change firewall/CDN rules or verify all technical causes of blocking, so you may need your web developer or hosting provider to implement the fixes.

When hiring, ask for **before-and-after tests for each crawler** and confirm which bots you want to allow. “AI crawlers” don’t all do the same thing: some support AI-powered search and citations; others may be used for model training. Allowing a bot also doesn’t guarantee that an assistant will mention your business.

content.text:
You’re looking for a **technical SEO or AI-search (AEO/GEO) specialist**—ideally someone who can audit and change the site, not just provide a visibility report. Ask them to check:

- `robots.txt` rules for relevant crawlers, such as **OAI-SearchBot / GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, and Google-Extended**
- Blocking by your hosting provider, CDN, firewall, or bot-protection settings
- Whether important pages render readable content without relying on JavaScript
- Sitemaps, page indexing settings, and structured data

A crawler-access checker can give you a quick initial read of the public `robots.txt` rules; the search results included options such as Apify’s **AI Crawler Access Checker**. But a checker usually can’t change firewall/CDN rules or verify all technical causes of blocking, so you may need your web developer or hosting provider to implement the fixes.

When hiring, ask for **before-and-after tests for each crawler** and confirm which bots you want to allow. “AI crawlers” don’t all do the same thing: some support AI-powered search and citations; others may be used for model training. Allowing a bot also doesn’t guarantee that an assistant will mention your business.
